0.content:
Broken Isle: Broken Isle is a limited-time island cluster in the west of the Golden Apple Archipelago, the summer-event map east of Mondstadt. Its main island has five peaks with differing water levels, linked to a group of rocks that ring a melody at high tide. It appeared in the Midsummer Island Adventure event (1.6) and again, redesigned, in Summertime Odyssey (2.8).

The island is event content, not part of the permanent world map. In both appearances it sat among hilichurl-held islands in sea fog.

Geography: The main island cluster has five peaks with varying water levels. The peaks are connected to a group of rocks, and when high tide presses the rocks down, the cluster rings with a melody. The people who once lived on the archipelago used this sound as a high-tide alarm.

History: Before the event the archipelago was known as the Haar Islands. The wooden ship on the unnamed island northeast of Broken Isle belongs to the Inazuma pirates of Ako Domeki's fleet, about 500 years ago: their boat split in two, and one group was shipwrecked on that Nameless Island between Broken Isle and Twinning Isle.

Dangers: Hilichurls and Hilichurl Berserkers and Fighters, elemental Samachurls, Hydro and Pyro slimes, a Hydro Abyss Mage, and elite Blazing Axe and Wooden Shieldwall Mitachurls (and a Stonehide Lawachurl in 1.6). Sea fog and shifting tides made the area hard to leave.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1. Both event runs ended (1.6 in June 2021, 2.8 in August 2022).

Treat it as a past summer-event location: characters may remember it, but it is no longer a place the Traveler can visit by ordinary exploration.

1.comment: Broken Isle: Broken Isle Tide Melody
1.content: Broken Isle's five peaks and rocks ring a melody when high tide presses the rocks down; the former inhabitants of the archipelago used it as a high-tide alarm. The island was a limited-time summer-event area in 1.6 and 2.8.

2.content:
Broken Sea: The Broken Sea is an area of Simulanka, the storybook world of the limited-time Summertide Scales and Tales event (4.8). It is unlocked during the quest Until the End of the World (Page III). People are stranded around it, and a boat there is one way to leave the book's world.

Visions do not work in Simulanka. Toy blocks and toy bombs shape its puzzles.

Geography: An area of sea and shore made of toy fixtures: Oracle Pillars that link in walkable lines, large Soaring Toys that launch the player, small Toy Blocks that can be assembled, Toy Bombs that destroy toytanium blocks, Toy Flowers that make wind currents when struck, and Toy Matches that burn a red toy block. During Page III the way to it on foot is blocked by an area boundary.

People: People are stranded around the Broken Sea. Kirara notes they are clearly stranded and that the stories never said the dragon had attacked their village; Nilou suggests they may be toytanium miners or guards who came for the dragon's head and could not leave.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; the event ended on 2024-08-28.

3.content: Alice says the boat at Simulanka's Broken Sea is one of two ways to leave the book's world; the other is a giant bookmark at the Cliff of Prophecy. Mini Durin is to help the stranded people near the sea go home.

4.content:
Constellation Metropole: Constellation Metropole is a royal city of toy figures in Simulanka, the storybook world of the limited-time Summertide Scales and Tales event (4.8). In the story Navia is its king, and the stars are missing from its sky. It has a Maritime Express station, a gear-driven lift and a statue of the Goddess of Prophecy.

Visions do not work in Simulanka. The Metropole is unlocked after Step 7 of the quest They Once Walked the Starry Sky (Page II).

Geography: A toy capital with a city highest point, a rail station for the Maritime Express, a Gear Sky Ladder (a lift raised by attacking a key mechanism), Oracle Pillars that connect in lines the player can walk, and "Superglue" that stops toy people and slows the player. A device called "Gift of the Goddess of Prophecy" lets the player rewind and replay time for certain puzzles and quests.

People: Navia reigns in the story; Bizerte and Montagne address her as Her Majesty and stay behind to look after the city when she sets off to slay the dragon with the Traveler, Nilou and the Wanderer. Wheel drives the Maritime Express. Kirara, who was in the Metropole, hears they have gone and follows.

History: Page II (They Once Walked the Starry Sky) has the party take the Maritime Express to the Metropole, save a toy man, follow Navia, capture a suspicious person from the city's highest point, shape Oracle Pillars and seek answers from the Goddess of Prophecy about the scattered stars (three to find).

Dangers: Hilichurls, including a Blazing Axe Mitachurl, seize a transfer platform on the way to the end of the world in Page III; in the city the hazards are mechanisms such as superglue.

Quests: The Metropole is the main setting of Page II and the starting point of Page III. Event minigames played here include the Metropole Trials, in which defeating opponents fills a Valor bar.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; the event ended on 2024-08-28.

5.comment: Constellation Metropole: Goddess of Prophecy statue
5.content: In Constellation Metropole, a statue of the Goddess of Prophecy holds a device that rewinds time for puzzles. In Page II the party consults her about the scattered stars.

6.content:
Cool Isle (also: Cool Isle realm layout): Cool Isle is one of the three Realm Layouts offered when the Serenitea Pot is first unlocked: a cluster of islands surrounded by water inside the teapot. The game's own blurb wonders how many cups of tea such a vast ocean could brew. It came with the Serenitea Pot in Version 1.5.

Its starting plateau is Pearl Isle; Conch-Court Isle, Mirage Isle and Letter Isle open as Trust Rank with Tubby rises. The mansion supplied is Mondstadt Mansion: Windward Manor. The Teapot Spirit Tubby and the travelling salesman Chubby appear here as in every layout.

Geography: Four islands set in open water, running from the starting island north and then northeast. Pearl Isle and Conch-Court Isle share the first island; Mirage Isle is the second island to the north; Letter Isle is the last island, in the northeast.

Places: Pearl Isle (Trust Rank 1): the starting area, a large plateau with a built-in Sub-Space Waypoint in its northwest. Conch-Court Isle (Rank 5): below Pearl Isle on the same island, with a large sandy area in the south and a smaller beach in the west. Mirage Isle (Rank 7): a long, narrow grassy building area. Letter Isle (Rank 9): the final island, with a large flat expanse.

Travel: Reached only by entering the Serenitea Pot gadget; once inside, the Sub-Space Waypoint and Mansion appear on the teapot map tab. Layouts are switched by speaking to Tubby, and furnishings in an inactive layout are kept.

Atmosphere: A bright, open island-and-sea setting, a neutral stage for tea, picnics and quiet conversation with companions, with Tubby fussing in the background.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 Cool Isle is unchanged since 1.5. Per the wiki it is available by default, or through the Trust Rank 8 and 10 layout unlocks.

7.content: Mondstadt Mansion: Windward Manor is the mansion furnishing supplied with Cool Isle. The wiki lists it as the layout's mansion; no lore is given.

8.comment: Cool Isle: Pearl Isle and Letter Isle
8.content: The four areas of Cool Isle: Pearl Isle (Trust Rank 1, starting plateau), Conch-Court Isle (5, beachy part of the first island), Mirage Isle (7, northern grassy strip) and Letter Isle (9, final northeastern island).

9.content:
Dark Sea (also: Dark Outer Sea, other-shore): The Dark Sea is Teyvat's name for everything beyond the continent and the Seven's dominion: unknown lands and seas, not only water. After the Archon War ended about 2,000 years ago, many defeated gods who refused to live under the Seven fled there and came to be called evil gods.

The name is a misnomer, since it covers landmasses as well as sea. Coastal peoples use it as a vague, ominous label for what lies past the edge of the known world; it is a term of folklore and item text rather than a charted place.

Geography: No map, boundary or list of regions exists. Canon describes the Dark Sea only as the regions outside the Seven Nations and outside the Seven's jurisdiction, including remote islands. Enkanomiya is the one place explicitly called part of it, even though it sits beneath Watatsumi Island and so within Teyvat's borders: the label is about who holds dominion, not distance.

People: The only inhabitants canon ties to the Dark Sea are the fled gods and, through Enkanomiya, the people who once lived in Byakuyakoku. Only one fled god is shown in detail: Orobashi, the serpent god, who met the abandoned people of Enkanomiya and chose to stay as their Orobashi no Mikoto, later returning to Teyvat to become the god of Watatsumi Island.

History: At the end of the Archon War, only the Seven remained and Teyvat took the form of the seven nations. Gods who would not live under the new order fled to islands in the Dark Sea. Other defeated gods took a different road and cooperated with the Seven, such as Boreas and Marchosius.

Atmosphere: In Teyvat the Dark Sea is a place of rumour: sea-monster legends in Liyue (where the term is rendered as the other-shore), warnings on the coasts, and dread of what refused the Seven. Characters speak of it as distant, dangerous and mostly unvisited.

Dangers: Canon gives no specific hazards beyond the old tales: sea monsters, hostile evil gods, and the unknown. Do not invent particular creatures.

Travel: Not accessible in the game and not visited in any quest, apart from Enkanomiya which is reached through a pool near Sangonomiya Shrine. Crossing to the Dark Sea is not described anywhere.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Dark Sea remains an undefined term. Nothing in Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content found for this entry redefines it.

10.comment: Dark Sea: Enkanomiya and the Dark Sea
10.content: Enkanomiya is called part of the Dark Sea in item text because it lay outside the Seven's jurisdiction. Its people, the lightless realm's inhabitants, were saved from the Dragonheirs of the Depths by the serpent god Orobashi, whom they worshipped. See the Enkanomiya entry for its history and the Orobashi entry for the god.

11.comment: Dark Sea: Gods who fled the Archon War
11.content: After the Archon War, gods who refused to live under the Seven fled to islands in the Dark Sea and came to be called evil gods. Others cooperated with the Seven instead. Only Orobashi is documented as a fled god. No other names are given in canon texts consulted.

12.content:
Domain (also: Domains, Secret Realm, Trounce Domain, Quest Domain, One-Time Domain, Domain of Blessing, Domain of Forgery, Domain of Mastery): Domains are self-contained pocket areas that adventurers enter through temple-like gateways, caves or broken structures scattered across Teyvat. Inside are combat trials, puzzles or powerful guardians, and at the end a reward. They are found in every region. Canon never explains in-world what they are, so treat them as mysterious, bounded places rather than a known institution.

Most are reached through a clearly marked entrance, which once discovered also serves travellers as a waypoint. The Adventurer Handbook presents them as trials that reward the brave with artifacts and materials for strengthening oneself.

Types: Game terms, not in-world classes. Challenge domains come in three kinds: Domains of Blessing (artifacts), Forgery (weapon ascension materials) and Mastery (talent materials). Trounce Domains hold exceptionally strong weekly bosses and open after the matching Archon or Story Quest. One-Time Domains give a set reward on first completion, and are often puzzles or small combat trials. Quest Domains appear only during a quest and cannot be revisited afterwards. Event Domains exist during limited-time events. The Spiral Abyss and the Imaginarium Theater are special rotating domains with their own entries.

Places: Domains sit in every region, from Mondstadt's ruined temples to ruins in Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru, Fontaine and Natlan. The Spiral Abyss opens through a wormhole in the sky at the edge of Cape Oath, and the Imaginarium Theater is reached from the Mondstadt Library at the Knights of Favonius Headquarters.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 domains remain a standard part of adventuring in every region.

Permanent domains, Trounce Domains and the rotating Spiral Abyss and Imaginarium Theater remain available. The wiki notes that no one-time domains have been added to any region since Version 3.6.

Gameplay: Gameplay description, not lore. Rewards from challenge and Trounce Domains are claimed with Original Resin, a resource that replenishes over time. Challenge domain stages rotate by weekday, and Sunday is open to all of them. Co-Op Mode allows others to join some domains, but not Quest Domains. Adventure Rank or particular quests unlock access: Blessing needs rank 22 or Song of the Dragon and Freedom, Forgery rank 16 or For a Tomorrow Without Tears, and Mastery rank 27 or Of the Land Amidst Monoliths.

13.content: At the end of a challenge domain, rewards are claimed at a petrified tree. Albedo remarks that these are considered young trees, while ancient ones would stand a mile or two high with an unknown kind of spider living in their roots. Canon has not shown such a tree, and does not say how they relate to Irminsul. Present this as a curiosity, not an established link.

14.content: Quest Domains exist only inside a specific quest and are sealed afterwards; One-Time Domains pay out once. Event Domains appear during limited-time events. During the Secret Summer Paradise event (limited), the lore repeatedly calls the Veluriyam Mirage a domain even though it behaves like a normal area.

15.content:
Emerald Peak (also: Emerald Peak realm layout): Emerald Peak is a mountain Realm Layout in the Serenitea Pot, one of the three offered by default. The game describes a cloud-piercing summit, then jokes that inside a teapot the tallest mountain probably reaches no higher than the stalk of a tea leaf. It was added in Version 1.5 with the Serenitea Pot.

Its four building areas are Spring Peak, Summerchase Peak, Autumnhold Peak and Wintersweep Peak, unlocked in that order through Trust Rank. The mansion supplied is the Liyue Estate: Exquisite Mansion, the same one Floating Abode uses.

Geography: A cluster of peaks with flat, buildable shoulders. Spring Peak is the largest flat area; Summerchase Peak is a pair of peaks beside it; Autumnhold Peak lies beyond a small intervening peak; Wintersweep Peak is the highest buildable ground.

Places: Spring Peak (Trust Rank 1): starting area and the largest flat space, with a Sub-Space Waypoint in the southwest. Summerchase Peak (Rank 5): two peaks beside Spring Peak; the northern one connects to Wintersweep. Autumnhold Peak (Rank 7): a large flat area with a smaller raised one above it. Wintersweep Peak (Rank 9): large, flat and the highest of the four.

Travel: Entered through the Serenitea Pot gadget and chosen via Tubby. Its Sub-Space Waypoint and Mansion appear on the teapot map tab. Chubby the salesman visits on Fridays to Sundays at one unlocked area.

Atmosphere: High and open, a summit setting with a Liyue-style estate. Good for contemplative or ceremonial scenes, with the running joke that the 'mountain' is tiny.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 Emerald Peak is unchanged since 1.5 and remains available by default or through the Trust Rank 8 and 10 layout unlocks.

16.comment: Emerald Peak: Spring Peak and Wintersweep Peak
16.content: The four areas of Emerald Peak in unlock order: Spring Peak (Trust Rank 1), Summerchase Peak (5), Autumnhold Peak (7) and Wintersweep Peak (9).

17.comment: Emerald Peak: Liyue Estate: Exquisite Mansion
17.content: The mansion furnishing given with both Emerald Peak and Floating Abode. It is listed as a Liyue-style estate; the game gives no history for it.

18.content:
Floating Abode (also: Floating Abode realm layout): Floating Abode is one of the three default Realm Layouts of the Serenitea Pot: a cluster of islands suspended in mid-air. The game calls this a typical feature of many adepti realms, a boundless world with nothing but a cluster of islands. It arrived in Version 1.5 with the Serenitea Pot.

The four isles are Windchill Isle, Cloudrest Isle, Smoke-Sailing Isle and Evermist Isle, linked in part by Adeptus Bridges. Its mansion is the Liyue Estate: Exquisite Mansion.

Geography: Four round, grassy islands floating in open sky, with trees on each. Windchill Isle has a large tree on its east side; Evermist Isle is the highest of the four and gives a view of the other three.

Places: Windchill Isle (Trust Rank 1): the starting isle, with an Adeptus Bridge to Cloudrest Isle on the west and a Sub-Space Waypoint in its northwest. Cloudrest Isle (Rank 5): joins Windchill to the east and Smoke-Sailing to the west. Smoke-Sailing Isle (Rank 7): joins Cloudrest to the north and Evermist to the south, with a rock pile and large tree in the northwest. Evermist Isle (Rank 9): the highest, linked to Smoke-Sailing by an Adeptus Bridge.

Travel: Entered via the Serenitea Pot gadget; layouts are changed by talking to Tubby. Chubby the Teapot Traveling Salesman appears at an unlocked isle on Fridays to Sundays.

Atmosphere: Calm, airy and a little otherworldly: a retreat held out of time, where the light outdoors never changes. It suits quiet talk, contemplation and tea.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 Floating Abode is unchanged since 1.5 and remains available by default or through Trust Rank 8 and 10 unlocks.

19.comment: Floating Abode: Windchill Isle and Evermist Isle
19.content: The four isles of Floating Abode in unlock order: Windchill Isle (Trust Rank 1), Cloudrest Isle (5), Smoke-Sailing Isle (7) and Evermist Isle (9), joined by Adeptus Bridges.

20.comment: Floating Abode: No Day or Night Outdoors
20.content: The wiki notes there is no visible day-night change outside in Floating Abode, so outdoor lights do not switch on; the Mansion interior still cycles. This is a gameplay observation, not a lore statement.

21.content:
Forest of Blessings (also: Kingdom of Breezes and Bells): The Forest of Blessings is the first area of Simulanka, the storybook world of the limited-time Summertide Scales and Tales event (4.8). Its wildlife is made of folded paper: frogs, hamsters, alpacas and flying squirrels. It holds the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells, a Hut of Blessings and a railway platform from which the Maritime Express runs to Constellation Metropole.

The Traveler and Paimon wake here after opening a strange book. Nilou helps the forest dwellers, and Visions do not work anywhere in Simulanka.

Geography: A green forest where paper creatures talk and sing, with ponds and waterfalls (Rainsong Pond), a large tree, the Hut of Blessings and a Calligraphy Tavern. The Kingdom of Breezes and Bells lies on a path from the hut and is reached through a big tree where flying squirrels offer gifts and talk of trials.

People: The paper residents are hamsters, frogs, alpacas and flying squirrels. They are friendly and quirky: a hamster guard with two alpaca attendants who speak for "the Boss", a hamster singer, hamsters hiding in barrels. Flying squirrels at the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells say the Princess is looking for a Guardian and ask whether visitors are there for the trials. Grandpa Almond, who needs a Magic Tonic, is one of the forest dwellers named in Page I.

History: Simulanka was made by Alice, Barbeloth and Andersdotter of the Hexenzirkel, whom its people know as the Goddesses of Creation, Prophecy and Fate. In Page III, M's journal in the Goddess of Fate's study says Alice's magic made one of M's origami frogs talk, which led M to imagine a story of paper animals in a magical forest.

Dangers: Large Hydro Slimes and a Tainted Hydro Phantasm frighten an alpaca near the path; Winged Dendroshrooms and floating Dendro and Hydro Fungi appear in the quest to collect materials for the Magic Tonic.

Quests: Page I, The Story Begins in a Forest Without Rain, opens the event: the Traveler wakes in the book, meets the forest dwellers, helps Nilou, collects tonic ingredients and gives the tonic to Grandpa Almond, then goes to the Calligraphy Tavern. Page II (They Once Walked the Starry Sky) starts at the forest's rail platform.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; the event ended on 2024-08-28.

22.comment: Forest of Blessings: Kingdom of Breezes and Bells
22.content: Within Simulanka's Forest of Blessings, the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells is where paper flying squirrels live. Its squirrels say the Princess is looking for a Guardian and ask visitors whether they come for the trials.

23.content:
Memory Core (also: Temple of Space: Memory Core): The Memory Core is a huge storage device at the centre of the Temple of Space, in the Pillar Hall Central Zone. It holds information about civilizations that have passed out of human memory. Travelers offer it Memory Factors, the ember-like remains of forgotten creations, and receive rewards in return.

The Temple of Space is the sky realm above Windrest Peak, shaped by Asmoday, the Lord of Emptiness. Its in-game description speaks of replicas of civilizations drifting in the instant before extinction, and says nobody can discern the realm's true purpose. The offering system bound to the Core carries its name, and the Core is reached after the quest The Wind Has Ceased.

Geography: The Core sits in the Pillar Hall Central Zone of the Temple of Space, a cold hall of silent pillars. The temple has its own map and exploration progress, separate from the main map of Teyvat.

Places: Around the Core are Josephus, who runs the Emberic Reconstruction shop, and (after the later quest) Istoria. Mnemonic Clusters and chests across the temple supply the Memory Factors brought here.

People: Two of the temple's "Uplifted" (people taken from past eras to be kept as living memories) are met here: Josephus, a philosopher of the era after the War of Funerary Flame, and Istoria, a philosopher of the unified civilization whose era came earlier. The two are friends.

Atmosphere: Silent, cold and still. Time stands still in the temple and its inhabitants do not age, tire or die. No wind is allowed into Asmoday's hall. The Core's maximum-level description is gentler: civilizations are fragile, yet remembering them still kindles hope for a slightly brighter tomorrow.

Travel: The Temple of Space is entered from a map marker at the Old Sanatorium Site after The Wind Has Ceased. Gameplay detail, not lore: Memory Factors are offered in groups of 20, 200 are needed for the maximum level, and some levels also require exploration progress in the temple. Rewards include Primogems, the achievement "Space and Unfree Will" and a namecard. At maximum level Emberic Reconstruction opens and excess Memory Factors can be traded to Josephus.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Core is open and in use. Josephus and Istoria remain in the temple.

24.content: Memory Factors are the fundamental building blocks of "Civilization". Anything made by a civilization that fades from collective memory eventually disintegrates into them. They are found in the Temple of Space, 3 from each floating Mnemonic Cluster and 1 from every chest except Remarkable Chests, and are offered at the Memory Core to receive blessings from the memories drifting in the interstices. Josephus calls them embers.

25.comment: Memory Core: Josephus and Emberic Reconstruction
25.content: Josephus is a philosopher from the era after the War of Funerary Flame who was uplifted to the Temple of Space. He is titled "Master of Anti-Self-Termination", a joke about a maths problem he posed on who ends up the last man standing among soldiers who refuse to surrender. He runs Emberic Reconstruction, a souvenir shop at the Memory Core that works once the Core is at its top level and takes Memory Factors as currency. He says nobody dies in the temple. He never heard of the dragon that tore open the sky, because his era came after Istoria's, when angels no longer gave humanity true secrets.

26.content: Istoria is a philosopher of the unified civilization who lived around the War of Funerary Flame, when Nibelung returned under the Abyss's influence about 6,000 years ago. He was among the first uplifted to the Temple of Space and spent centuries in the Apathic Interval first. He is the first Uplifted the Traveler and Paimon meet in A Long Day in the Mountains, and he asks for help to free the temple. He is a friend of Josephus and is met at the Memory Core after that quest.

27.content:
Minacious Isle: Minacious Isle is a limited-time island in the southwest of the Golden Apple Archipelago. According to Albedo, its main island used to be a mountain of Mondstadt that was ripped away and landed in the sea upside down. It has inverted ruins, dandelions, Anemo enemies and a way back to Mondstadt, and appeared in the 1.6 and 2.8 summer events.

Its Mondstadt origin fits the nation of Anemo: the island has Anemo slimes and an Eye of the Storm, and the quest The Winding Homeward Way ends at a portal to Mondstadt.

Geography: A main island with the Inverted Ruins, dandelions, windmill mechanisms and wind currents, a northwest island, and a small stray island far to the west. A whirlpool just west of the main island leads into an underwater ruin cave.

History: In the event's Echoing Tales conch narration, Albedo tells that Barbatos reshaped Mondstadt, splitting mountaintops that landed in the sea upside down. The wiki's archipelago timeline puts the island's arrival at the Haar Islands, with a Seelie, less than about 2,600 years ago. A shipwrecked group afterwards settled across the archipelago. An eroded tablet in the underwater ruins calls the place an observation point suited to astronomical research.

Dangers: Anemo, Hydro, Pyro, Cryo and Dendro slimes of several sizes, hilichurls and shamans of various elements, Hilichurl Grenadiers and shooters, shield guards, and elite Blazing Axe, Stonehide Lawachurl and Wooden Shieldwall chieftains, along with an Eye of the Storm.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; it existed only during the 1.6 and 2.8 event runs.

Characters may speak of it as the island that came from Mondstadt, but nothing in released canon places the Traveler there after the events ended.

28.comment: Minacious Isle: Minacious Isle Inverted Ruins
28.content: Minacious Isle's Inverted Ruins stand upside down because, by Albedo's account, the island was a Mondstadt mountain broken off and flipped into the sea. The island has dandelions, Anemo creatures and a portal home to Mondstadt (the quest The Winding Homeward Way).

29.content:
Nod-Krai (also: Nephilheim, Nod Krai, Nod-Kraian): Nod-Krai is an autonomous region on the southernmost edge of Snezhnaya, in Teyvat's northwest: cold islands, desolate tundra, snowy groves and long, dark nights. It has no Archon and no true government. People from all over Teyvat gather in its scrap-metal port, Nasha Town, which gives the land a reputation as a lawless "Elysium". The Frostmoon Scions, its indigenous people, worship the Moon Goddess Kuutar, the former Fatui Harbinger Columbina. The land is soaked in kuuvahki, the power of the moons, and since the Cataclysm it has been plagued by the Abyssal Wild Hunt.

The main powers are the Voynich Guild merchants, the Lightkeepers militia, the Frostmoon Scions and Nefer's Curatorium of Secrets. Nod-Krai is the setting of the Archon Quest Song of the Welkin Moon (6.0-6.3), and its great festival is Moon-Prayer Night.

Geography: Nod-Krai is a chain of islands surrounded by sea. Most people live in the Southern Isles: Lempo Isle (Nasha Town), Hiisi Island (the Scions' forest home) and Paha Isle (the Fatui's Design Bureau and the Final Night Cemetery). To the north lies the large island of Pohjola: Voidsea Outlook with the Lightkeepers' city Piramida, Wavechaser Plain, Ashveil Peak in the far north, and Dunanna Pit near Fontaine.

Government: Nobody rules Nod-Krai. Shortly after the Cataclysm, about 500 years ago, the Tsaritsa (Anastasya) approved Solovei's request to make it an autonomous region, with the Lightkeepers given jurisdiction to defend it. In practice the Voynich Guild, a merchants' guild in Nasha Town, is the closest thing to a regulator.

Religion: The Frostmoon Scions worship the Frost Moon. They honour the late goddess Canon as Huurrekuutar and her successor Kuutar (Columbina), who was born about 500 years ago, and they carved Statues of the New Moon in her image all over Nod-Krai. Most townsfolk care little for the religion.

Economy: Nasha Town is the main port and trading centre. Nod-Krai has few resources, so much of the town is built from scrap metal, with cargo rails overhead and kuuvahki-powered machines on every corner. Adventuring, salvage and trade drive the economy.

Military: The Lightkeepers, a volunteer militia founded about 500 years ago by Solovei, the first Torchforger, hold back the Wild Hunt. They are based in Piramida and led by a Starshyna, currently Nikita, and they are badly understrength.

History: In the Natlantean era the land was called Nephilheim. Nibelung raised the Three Moons here, and Nod-Krai is said to be made from material left over from their making. After a Celestial Nail destroyed the northern realm of Hyperborea, the Frost Moon goddess Canon led its survivors to Hiisi Island before she died; their descendants are the Frostmoon Scions. Nod-Krai was the first land struck by the Cataclysm after Khaenri'ah fell. The Wild Hunt arose from Rerir, one of the Five Sinners, and the Khaenri'ahn exile Rotwang tried to open the false sky to the Abyss until the Scion leader Aila and the Snezhnayan noble Solovei stopped him.

Dangers: The Wild Hunt is a host of ghouls made from the dead, tainted by Abyssal energy. It is far stronger here than anywhere else. A beaten-down ghoul becomes "grief-stricken" and must be worn down again before it truly falls. The Hunt rarely goes to Hiisi Island because the moon's power deters it. Kipumaki Cliff in the far north is the worst hotspot.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Nod-Krai is at peace again and rebuilding. Dottore was destroyed in the Song of the Welkin Moon crisis. The real Frost Moon has been pulled back inside Teyvat's sky, and Columbina lives openly among the Frostmoon Scions on Hiisi Island. The Wild Hunt has lost its leaders but still roams. The Traveler has moved on to Snezhnaya.

The Tsaritsa revoked the Palestar Edict against Columbina, Sandrone apologised to the Scions on the Fatui's behalf, and the factions founded a joint League. Rerir is outside Teyvat in the moon's reflection, and Rotwang is gone for good. At the start of Chapter VII (7.0), Columbina threw the Traveler a farewell party at the Flagship before they left for Snezhnaya.

30.content: The Southern Isles are the most populated part of Nod-Krai apart from Piramida. Lempo Isle holds Nasha Town, the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop (Aino's home and workshop) and Starsand Shoal. Hiisi Island is the Frostmoon Scions' home: largely untouched forest with the Frostmoon Enclave, the Light-Bathed Platform with a giant statue of Kuutar, and the only Statue of the New Moon the Fatui never defaced. Its hidden grotto, Silvermoon Hall, is where Columbina hid under Lauma's protection. Paha Isle is the Fatui staging ground, home to the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, and also holds the Final Night Cemetery, a graveyard isle of fallen Lightkeepers.

31.comment: Nod-Krai: Pohjola and the Far North
31.content: Pohjola is the great island north of the Southern Isles. It opened in 6.3, except for Dunanna Pit, which opened in 6.7. Voidsea Outlook at its southern end holds Piramida, the Lightkeepers' city, built on a mountain around a giant Hyperborean lighthouse over the ruins of Prokhor Trubetskoy's castle, as well as Dreadshade Mire. Wavechaser Plain holds the Pillar of Embla, Lake Amsvartnir and the Knights' Favonius Keep. Ashveil Peak, in the far north, holds Kipumaki Cliff and the Lightkeepers' Cliffwatch Camp. Dunanna Pit lies near Fontaine, east of Pohjola.

32.comment: Nod-Krai: Nephilheim, Hyperborea and the Three Moons
32.content: Nod-Krai was called Nephilheim in Natlantean times. Nibelung created the Three Moons here: the Eternal, Frost and Iridescent Moons, each with a goddess (Aria, Canon and Sonnet). In the war against the Heavenly Principles, the Eternal and Iridescent Moons were shattered and the Frost Moon was flung beyond the false sky. When Hyperborea in the far north was destroyed by a Celestial Nail, Canon, out of pity, led its survivors to Nod-Krai before she died. They raised a tower and preserved Hyperborean devices in the hope that a reborn Frost Moon would let them return home.

33.content: A Fatui stronghold in Nod-Krai belonged to Dottore. Its public face, the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau on Paha Isle, was run by Sandrone ("Marionette"), Seventh of the Harbingers. The Fatui pulled down two Ancient Moon remnants, caged or defaced Statues of the New Moon, pressed the Scions to give up Columbina, and pursued her under the Palestar Edict. Locals resented them deeply. Some rank-and-file Fatui, such as Jotautas and Gediminas, later helped the heroes against Dottore.

34.comment: Nod-Krai: The Song of the Welkin Moon Crisis
34.content: The Traveler came to Nasha Town with Ineffa at Varka's invitation, sensing a power like the one they felt when their spaceship landed. The Eternal Moon Marrow was stolen, and Rerir, master of the Wild Hunt, murdered the Lightkeeper Sousi and framed Flins. Rerir then tricked the town into firing Aino's cannon so that it rebuilt his body. Allies including Lauma, Flins, Nefer, Jahoda, Aino, Ineffa, Varka, Columbina, Arlecchino, Albedo, Durin and Dainsleif cast him out of Teyvat through a moon gate. As Moon-Prayer Night neared, Columbina began fading because she had no true name. The Traveler named her, and she became Columbina Hyposelenia. At her farewell, Dottore seized the three moons' power, and she vanished into the moon's reflection.

35.content:
Pudding Isle: Pudding Isle is a limited-time island in the east of the Golden Apple Archipelago, the summer-event map east of Mondstadt. It was the island where the player started in Midsummer Island Adventure (1.6) and, in Summertime Odyssey (2.8), an island whose halves a bonsai could switch between Mondstadt, Liyue and Inazuma styles.

Canon records no residents or history of its own for the island; it is known only through the events.

Geography: In 1.6 the first island players landed on held a teleport waypoint, a Door of Resurrection, a waverider waypoint and two Echoing Conches. A main island lay beyond, with a Stonehide Lawachurl guarding a chest, plus a southeast islet of Hymnal Rings and a peaked islet to the northeast.

History: The island belongs to the Haar Islands, the archipelago's older name. Its Echoing Conches in 1.6 carried recorded voices of earlier visitors (titles include "The General" and "The Price of Experimentation"); more conches appeared after Act III.

Dangers: Hilichurls, slimes and elite guardians such as a Stonehide Lawachurl (1.6) and a Bloatty Floatty drifting near the main island.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; limited to the 1.6 and 2.8 event runs.

36.content: Pudding Isle in the 2.8 Summertime Odyssey event could be restyled by a bonsai: each half switched among Mondstadt, Liyue and Inazuma versions, with matching elemental monuments (Anemo, Geo, Electro) and Seelie puzzles.

37.content:
Shadowflit Archipelago (also: Shadowflit Archipelago realm layout): Shadowflit Archipelago is the Nod-Krai-themed Realm Layout of the Serenitea Pot, added in Version Luna V (6.4, released 2026-02-25). The game describes a complicated group of islands hovering high in the sky, drawn together by some mysterious mechanism.

It is unlocked with the Sphere of Fleeting Shadow, bought from Tubby at the Realm Depot. The sphere is a Nod-Krai kuuvahki mechanism that plays music and produces dazzling light, a souvenir Chubby brought from Nod-Krai. The mansion is the Kerplunk-a-tron Windmill Base, and the four areas are Vassen Isle, Troki Isle, Ettu Isle and Vietje Isle.

Geography: Islands hovering high in the sky and held together by an unexplained mechanism. The wiki has no further area descriptions.

Places: Vassen Isle (Trust Rank 1), Troki Isle (Rank 5), Ettu Isle (Rank 7) and Vietje Isle (Rank 9). The wiki has not yet described them.

Travel: Entered through the Serenitea Pot gadget after the sphere is used and then chosen with Tubby. Chubby, the sphere's supplier, appears at an unlocked area on Fridays to Sundays.

Atmosphere: Airy, gleaming and faintly mechanical, with soft shifting light. It suits scenes of wonder and curiosity about Nod-Krai's kuuvahki, in a place with no Fatui or Abyss threat.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 it is the most recently added Realm Layout and unchanged since Luna V.

38.comment: Shadowflit Archipelago: Sphere of Fleeting Shadow
38.content: The item that unlocks Shadowflit Archipelago: a Nod-Krai kuuvahki sphere mechanism that plays music and produces dazzling light effects, brought back by Chubby as a souvenir. It is bought from Tubby in the Realm Depot.

41.content:
Silken Courtyard (also: Silken Courtyard realm layout): Silken Courtyard is an Inazuma-themed Realm Layout added to the Serenitea Pot in Version 2.2. The game says its charm comes from overlapping patchworks of mountains and waters and the elegant scent of tea in the air. It is unlocked with the Silken Print, a prayer plaque of Inazuman scenery carved on Yumemiru wood.

The print is a Level 40 reward of Sacred Sakura's Favor, the offering system at the Sacred Sakura of Grand Narukami Shrine. The layout's mansion is the Inazuman Walled House: Refined Estate. Its four areas are Kasumi Shoal, Madoromi Island, Sakurazaki Island and Nodoka Terrace.

Geography: Four islands of beach, grass and cliff linked by trails, a wooden bridge and a bridge of sakura petals, with sakura trees.

Places: Kasumi Shoal (Trust Rank 1): a sandy starting beach with a sakura tree and a Sub-Space Waypoint in the west; a non-buildable island behind it has a trail to Madoromi Island. Madoromi Island (Rank 5): round and flat, with cliffs facing Kasumi Shoal; a sakura petal bridge leads to Sakurazaki Island. Sakurazaki Island (Rank 7): lower than Madoromi, with a small beach and steep cliffs; a wooden bridge leads on to Nodoka Terrace. Nodoka Terrace (Rank 9): a cliff-top building area above a southern beach.

Travel: Reached through the Serenitea Pot gadget once the Silken Print has been obtained; the layout is then switched via Tubby. Chubby visits one unlocked area on Fridays to Sundays.

Atmosphere: Elegant and unhurried, scented with tea and sakura. A natural stage for a refined Inazuman tea gathering, in a realm with no Shogunate and no Vision hunts.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 unchanged since 2.2. It stays unlocked via the Silken Print rather than being a default layout.

42.content: The item that unlocks Silken Courtyard: a prayer plaque showing Inazuman scenery, carved on Yumemiru wood in full colour. It is a Level 40 reward of Sacred Sakura's Favor.

43.comment: Silken Courtyard: Kasumi Shoal and Nodoka Terrace
43.content: The four areas of Silken Courtyard: Kasumi Shoal (Trust Rank 1), Madoromi Island (5), Sakurazaki Island (7) and Nodoka Terrace (9).

45.content:
Simulanka: Simulanka is a storybook world created by the Hexenzirkel witches Alice, Barbeloth and Andersdotter, whom its people call the Goddesses of Creation, Prophecy and Fate. In the limited 4.8 event Summertide Scales and Tales, a strange book sent by Alice pulled the Traveler, Paimon and several friends into it to save the world from an evil dragon. Visions do not work there.

The dragon turned out to be Durin, a gentle storybook creation of the Goddess of Fate whose touch turns things into toy blocks. Nilou, Navia, Kirara and the Wanderer gave him their blessings, and he became a small, harmless dragon. Alice then told the party how Simulanka was founded and how they could leave.

Geography: Three subareas make up the world. The Forest of Blessings is where visitors first arrive, a woodland whose creatures are made of folded paper. Constellation Metropole is a city of tracks, gears and toy figures, reached by train. The Broken Sea is at the far end of the world, where a mining village of stranded workers and guards lives near the dragon's waterfall lair.

People: The Forest of Blessings is inhabited by origami animals such as paper frogs, hamsters, alpacas and flying squirrels. Nilou is cast as the Fairy of the Forest in the story's prophecy, and the villagers include Almond, Ginkgo and Chestnut. Navia is cast as the King of Constellation Metropole, with ministers Montagne and Bizerte. The Maritime Express is driven by Wheel. Kirara and the Wanderer ('Hat Guy') arrive separately, the Wanderer bearing the title Hero of Simulanka.

Governance: No fixed government is shown. Navia is told by a voice that she is the king of Constellation Metropole and plays the role; Nilou's role is Fairy of the Forest. These are story roles given to visitors, not permanent offices.

Culture: Life in Simulanka follows the three goddesses. The Goddess of Creation gave life to matter and magic and folded storybook pages into the Forest's animals. The Goddess of Prophecy rules the stars and the natural course of things, and the Metropole's machinery is described as her gift for keeping people on track, though residents keep personal freedom. The Goddess of Fate presides over cherished stories and wishes, and visitors tell her their wishes at the end of the world.

History: Alice, Barbeloth and Andersdotter created Simulanka together. Alice (Goddess of Creation) proposed stepping into the worlds in Andersdotter's stories; Barbeloth (Goddess of Prophecy) mapped the fate of all living things; and Andersdotter, 'M', the Goddess of Fate, wrote the tales. Andersdotter wrote a story set among origami animals, and also the story of a young dragon.

Dangers: Near the dragon his breath makes full power impossible (the party could not use Elemental Skills and Bursts in the final fight). The Wanderer says the fog around can cause hallucinations; the dragon's attack also made the party witness his memories. Hilichurls seized one train platform. Visions do not work anywhere in Simulanka; the story's own 'magic' replaces them.

Travel: Visitors arrive by opening a book Alice sent them, not by any road. Within the world one travels by the Maritime Express. To leave, one takes the boat at the Broken Sea or touches the giant bookmark at the Cliff of Prophecy and concentrates on the destination; Alice noted the way home was available from the beginning, though no one told the party.

Quests: The story of Summertide Scales and Tales has three pages and an afterword: the Forest of Blessings and the closed tavern, the trip to the Metropole to ask the Goddess of Prophecy, and the train to the end of the world to face the evil dragon. Four mini-games supplied the gameplay: Boreal Flurry, Flying Hatter's Trick, Metropole Trials and Figurine Fabrication.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Simulanka is not accessible. Durin lives in Mondstadt as a playable character (6.2). Alice has since appeared in person elsewhere in the story, but not in Simulanka.

46.content: Simulanka's people call Alice the Goddess of Creation, Barbeloth the Goddess of Prophecy and Andersdotter ('M') the Goddess of Fate. Alice tells the party that the three contributed equally to founding the world. The Goddess of Fate is described as M's reflection who grants wishes and loves cliffhangers. The Goddess of Prophecy is statued at the highest point of Constellation Metropole.

47.content: The 'evil dragon' of Simulanka is Durin, a gentle storybook creation of the Goddess of Fate who was shunned and hunted by Simulanka's people. He took the stars after M's death and could turn things to toy blocks. The Wanderer reached him in the dragon's memories and told him his name. The party's blessings freed him from the curse and he became Mini Durin. His later story is in Durin's own entry.

48.content: Simulanka's origami woodland, where the Hut of Blessings stands and where the Goddess of Creation first made the townspeople. Its tavern was closed until Nilou learned the magic of the Goddess of Creation. Its animals are made of paper and fear the dragon.

49.content: Simulanka's gear-driven toy city, ruled in the story by Navia as king, with a Goddess of Prophecy statue at its summit and the Astral Garden. Its stars were scattered when the dragon took them. Routes include the Gear Sky Ladder and the Maritime Express station.

50.content: The end of Simulanka's world, where workers from the toytanium mines and would-be dragon-slayers are stranded near a waterfall, behind which lies the dragon's lair. A boat here can carry travellers to another world.

51.content:
Skirk's Planet (also: Skirk's homeland, Skirk's home planet): Skirk's planet is the world in the sea of stars where the swordswoman Skirk was born. It began as a hostile world whose extreme temperatures could not support life, yet humans emerged there and evolved the ability to adapt to any environment or energy source. A merchant ship from a neighbouring planet was welcomed, discovered that ability and judged the people a threat, and an army then destroyed them. The planet is unnamed and cannot be visited; it is known only from Skirk's memories in her Crystallina Chapter (5.7).

Skirk survived only because Surtalogi, one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, took her in and trained her. She later travelled to Teyvat, and she still carries her homeland's tunes and instruments.

Geography: The planet once lacked the conditions for life because of extreme temperatures. By Skirk's childhood it carried grasses and forests, a sea with large fish and treasures at the bottom, a northern prairie, and a giant bird said to spit fire.

People: Humans who, over generations, evolved the ability to adapt to nearly any environment or energy source. The wiki reads this as letting them touch the Abyss without grave danger, though none ever used it as a power. They lived in villages, sent children to school, and welcomed visitors with hospitality.

Culture: Her people made music, and Skirk keeps a tune her parents taught her. The item "Lingering Euphonia" is a guitar Skirk made from the instruments of her homeland, with an ancient melody that seems to hum of a history nobody recalls.

History: A merchant ship from a neighbouring planet arrived while Skirk was a child. The locals welcomed the crew, who explored the planet and learned that the people could adapt to any environment or energy source. The outsiders judged them a potential threat. Months later an army of unknown origin landed without warning and set about destroying everything and everyone. Skirk's village was burned; her wounded parents told her to flee, and soldiers left her under burning rubble. She survived only through Surtalogi's intervention.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 the planet is destroyed and is seen only in Skirk's memories. Skirk has not returned, and canon gives no way to travel there.

Atmosphere: Treat it as a memory, tender and grieving: grass, sea and stars seen through a child's eyes, ending in smoke. Skirk speaks of it rarely and without drama.

52.comment: Skirk's Planet: The Merchant Ship and the Razing
52.content: In Skirk's memories a spaceship of outsiders who spoke of friendship arrived and was welcomed. Their investigation showed the planet's people could adapt to any environment or energy source, so they were treated as a potential threat. An army came months later and destroyed the people. Soldiers spoke of burning the civilisation down; most villagers were unable to resist.

53.comment: Skirk's Planet: Adaptation and the Abyss
53.content: Her people's adaptability allowed contact with the Abyss without grave danger, though they never used it directly. Skirk's own power came later from Surtalogi's training, and she hides it in Teyvat as Cryo through the Seven-Shifting Serpent technique.

54.content: Skirk told the Traveler she is not from Teyvat but from a different planet, and that she once journeyed through the stars. The planet is unnamed. Her own entry carries her personal story; this entry covers the place.

55.content:
Sublime Spicewood (also: Sublime Spicewood realm layout): Sublime Spicewood is the Sumeru-themed Realm Layout, added in Version 3.2. The game pictures the branches and leaves of a towering tree hanging high above a sea of clouds, immense and sturdy, with a wondrous floral fragrance lingering evermore.

It unlocks by completing the Archon Quest Secret of the Scorching Desert and buying Nature's True Fruit from Tubby at the Realm Depot. The fruit is a fragrant memento Chubby brought back from Sumeru. The mansion is the Sumeru Mansion: Meditative Retreat; the four areas are Reverie Realm, Seat of Clarity, In Wit's Corner and Dais of Wisdom.

Geography: A canopy-top landscape of branches and leaves above cloud. Elevation falls from the Reverie Realm, the highest area, to In Wit's Corner, the lowest.

Places: Reverie Realm (Trust Rank 1): the highest area, with a small pond to the east and a Sub-Space Waypoint in the south. Seat of Clarity (Rank 5): a round area surrounded by vines. In Wit's Corner (Rank 7): the lowest area, with the built-in fish pond along the path from Seat of Clarity. Dais of Wisdom (Rank 9): a round area with a small pond on its west side.

Travel: Reached via the Serenitea Pot gadget after buying and using Nature's True Fruit; switched via Tubby. Chubby appears at one unlocked area on Fridays to Sundays.

Atmosphere: Fragrant, lofty and hushed, a treetop retreat suited to study, meditation or a Sumeru-flavoured tea party.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 unchanged since 3.2; it is still unlocked by the quest-gated fruit rather than by default.

56.content: The item that unlocks Sublime Spicewood. Its text calls it a marvellously fragrant fruit that Chubby brought from Sumeru, whose scent calls up images the pot's Sub-Space Creation can recreate. It is bought from Tubby in the Realm Depot after Secret of the Scorching Desert.

57.comment: Sublime Spicewood: Reverie Realm and Dais of Wisdom
57.content: The four areas of Sublime Spicewood: Reverie Realm (Trust Rank 1), Seat of Clarity (5), In Wit's Corner (7) and Dais of Wisdom (9).

58.comment: Sublime Spicewood: Sumeru Mansion: Meditative Retreat
58.content: The mansion furnishing supplied with Sublime Spicewood; the game offers no lore beyond its name.

59.content:
Swirling Isles (also: Swirling Isles realm layout): Swirling Isles is the Fontaine-themed Realm Layout, added in Version 4.3: a wondrous deepwater archipelago, silent and serene, with a multitude of lights swirling about. Inside the realm it is always night, whatever hour the clock shows.

It unlocks after the Archon Quest Lies Cast Shadows Under Gathered Lights, by buying the Swirling Scene in a Bottle from Tubby at the Realm Depot. The bottle is a terrarium of landscapes Chubby brought back from Fontaine. The mansion is the Fontaine Villa: Illusory Annex, and the four areas are Luminescent Islet, Seafoam Shoal, Brumerose Reef and Clearbreak Surf.

Geography: Islands scattered across deep, still water with lights drifting around them. Brumerose Reef, the third area, has a built-in Ornamental Fish pond at the far end of its island that functions like a Pool of Sapphire Grace without counting against load.

Places: Luminescent Islet (Trust Rank 1): the starting area. Seafoam Shoal (Rank 5). Brumerose Reef (Rank 7): has the built-in fish pond. Clearbreak Surf (Rank 9). Each takes up to 16,000 load.

Travel: Reached through the Serenitea Pot gadget once the bottle has been used, then selected through Tubby. Chubby, whose trip to Fontaine the item text mentions, appears at one unlocked area on Fridays to Sundays.

Atmosphere: Hushed night-time water with drifting lights: a dreamy setting suited to quiet, intimate or reflective scenes. It borrows Fontaine's look, but canon states no courtroom, Oratrice or Hydro Archon presence here.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 unchanged since 4.3 and still unlocked through the quest-gated bottle.

60.comment: Swirling Isles: Swirling Scene in a Bottle
60.content: The item that unlocks Swirling Isles: a terrarium of lovely landscapes Chubby brought from Fontaine, whose scenes the pot's Sub-Space Creation can recreate. It is bought from Tubby after Lies Cast Shadows Under Gathered Lights.

61.comment: Swirling Isles: Always Night in the Realm
61.content: In Swirling Isles it is always night, whatever time the clock shows; companions give only night greetings and the time cannot be changed from inside the Realm Within. This is a recorded gameplay behaviour.

62.comment: Swirling Isles: Luminescent Islet and Clearbreak Surf
62.content: The four areas of Swirling Isles: Luminescent Islet (Trust Rank 1), Seafoam Shoal (5), Brumerose Reef (7, with a built-in fish pond) and Clearbreak Surf (9).

63.comment: Swirling Isles: Fontaine Villa: Illusory Annex
63.content: The mansion furnishing supplied with Swirling Isles; no lore is given beyond its name.

64.content:
Temple of Space (also: Segment-Domain Tau, Hall of Emptiness): The Temple of Space, which its maker named "Segment-Domain Tau", is a vast temple floating unseen in the sky above Windrest Peak in northern Mondstadt. It belongs to Asmoday, the Ruler of Space. She turned it into an exhibition hall for vanished civilisations. People, relics, landscapes and even whole ecosystems from past ages were "uplifted" into it and kept there, unchanging, as living memories. Inside, time stands still: nobody ages, hungers, tires or dies. Asmoday has been gone for a long time. The Watcher Melanta then ruled the temple harshly until the Traveler defeated him in 6.5.

The way in is the Statue of The Seven at the Old Sanatorium Site, a ruined building on Windrest Peak that stands on what the temple left behind on the ground. Loading-screen lore says wind may not enter the Master of Space's hall, which is why the mountain winds below are so fierce.

Geography: The temple is a huge structure of halls, walkways and display cases hanging above the clouds over Windrest Peak. Paimon is amazed that something so big floats over Mondstadt without anyone seeing it. Its centre is the Pillar Hall of Space, where the Watchers once kept watch over the world. Around it are three themed exhibition areas: Luyang Academy, the Mahavaipulya Chamber and the Desert Pavilion. At its highest point is the Cage (Atrium) of Suchness, home of Asmoday and her Watchers. The Corridor of Nothingness separates the Cage from the lower, inhabited temple, which is called the Hall of Emptiness. Below and apart from it all is the Apathic Interval, a transitional space.

Governance: Asmoday made the temple a place of preservation only. She created two Watchers, Nihilita and Melanta, to keep order from the Cage of Suchness, bring chosen people in and observe Teyvat in silence. She also made the Domain Keepers as lesser guardians. Her rule forbade innovation and change of any kind. Leaving was possible only by building the Path to the Heavens, which costs all of one's memories, so that nothing learned in the temple could return to the mortal world.

History: The people of Great Arcadia worshipped both the Master of Time (Istaroth) and the Master of Space (Asmoday), and raised a temple to each; the two were once joined. A loading screen says Asmoday never visited while the temple flourished. After a disaster the Temple of Space was lifted into the sky and hidden, and only then did her gaze rest on it. She remade it into Segment-Domain Tau, a silent watchtower over the world. The ruins on the ground were later built over into the sanatorium. At some point Asmoday vanished. Nihilita "opened his eye", left his post and was branded a traitor. Melanta stayed and enforced her rules ever more harshly.

Quests: The temple is the setting of the world quest series A Long Day in the Mountains (6.5). It begins with The Wind Has Ceased at Dornman Port and the Old Sanatorium Site and continues through Luyang Academy, the Mahavaipulya Chamber, the Desert Pavilion and the Apathic Interval. It ends with the confrontation with Melanta in The Final Judgment.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the temple is free of Melanta's rule and still floats hidden above Windrest Peak, with its uplifted residents still living there. Asmoday has not returned.

Melanta self-destructed after his defeat. Nihilita is out in the mortal world. Istoria remains at the Memory Core. Dex, the juvenile Watcher the residents raised, keeps helping the Traveler explore the temple (in gameplay terms, its manipulation abilities stay available).

65.comment: Temple of Space: The Uplifted and the Apathic Interval
65.content: "Uplifted" is the temple's term for people taken from a particular era or a vanished civilisation and preserved there forever as living memories. The Watchers first cast them into the Apathic Interval. To leave it, a person must give up every desire through meditation and mastery of their thoughts until their mind is completely empty, which takes anywhere from a few years to several centuries. The process changes their personality and stops them from ever gaining a Vision. Once inside, they no longer age, hunger, tire or die. Istoria says the uplifting is thought to have ended.

66.comment: Temple of Space: The Watchers Nihilita and Melanta
66.content: Asmoday created two Watchers to keep the temple and named them after the two things she could least bear: Nihilita (nothingness) and Melanta (melancholy). After she vanished, Nihilita "opened his eye", saw the truths of the world and left, so Melanta called him the traitor, the Fallen One. Melanta stayed in the Cage of Suchness and tried to restore the original rules by punishing the residents. Nihilita waited on Windrest Peak for someone who could free the temple. He sent first Raumhilda and then the Traveler, each time lending them the juvenile Watcher Dex.

67.comment: Temple of Space: Path to the Heavens and the Corridor of Nothingness
67.content: The Corridor of Nothingness separates the inhabited Hall of Emptiness from the Cage (Atrium) of Suchness at the temple's summit. The only way to an audience with the temple's master, and so the only way out, is to build the Path to the Heavens across the Corridor by giving up all of one's memories and wisdom, so that the temple's truths never reach the mortal world. Walkers on the Path get one last look back at their memories. With Asmoday gone, a path once built does not vanish after use. Melanta, however, destroyed half of the Corridor and cut the Path that Raumhilda had built.

68.comment: Temple of Space: Raumhilda and Zeitlind in the Temple
68.content: Raumhilda ("Hilda") met Nihilita on a midnight walk while she was staying at the Windrest Peak sanatorium. He entrusted Dex to her and sent her to the temple, where she befriended the residents (she called Istoria "Grandpa"). She also learned painting from Daozi and Bosch. Moved by the residents' suffering, she gave up her memories to build the Path to the Heavens and faced Melanta. They could not agree, and she promised that her younger sister would one day come and defeat him. She left with no memories, and her grave at the sanatorium is empty. Her younger sister Zeitlind later came looking for her, and with the Traveler she freed the temple and paid the same price in memories.

69.comment: Temple of Space: Shades' Additions to the Temple
69.content: Asmoday's rule was pure preservation, but after she vanished her sister Shades softened it. They brought in things they liked and allowed small acts of change. Luyang Academy, a segment of ancient Liyue, grew into a working art school. The Mahavaipulya Chamber filled with new novels by residents. Naberius, Ronova and Istaroth commissioned Venipi to rebuild a Sumeru desert complex from memory, which became the Desert Pavilion. Melanta treated all of this as corruption and punished it until the Traveler restored each hall.

70.content:
Teyvat: Teyvat is the world of the story, a planet and the continent on it, where the seven elements (Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro, Hydro, Pyro, Cryo) flow. It has seven nations, each tied to one element, one ideal and one god of The Seven (the Archons): Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru, Fontaine, Natlan and Snezhnaya. Above it floats Celestia, seat of the Heavenly Principles, who have ruled the world since conquering it in the distant past. Ordinary people may receive a Vision that lets them wield an element. 500 years ago the fall of the godless underground kingdom Khaenri'ah, the cataclysm, unleashed the Abyss on every nation. That calamity has ended, but peace has not fully returned.

Most people know Teyvat simply as the world of the Archons and Celestia. Few know the truth: the visible sky is a false sky, a shell around the planet, and the true cosmos beyond it is called the sea of stars.

Geography: In official descriptions, Mondstadt lies in the northeast, Liyue is a harbor nation in the east, Inazuma is an isolated archipelago far to the east bordering the Dark Sea, Sumeru is in the west-central part of the continent, Fontaine is a "terrestrial sea" in the center, Natlan lies in the western regions and Snezhnaya is the land of eternal winter in the north. Nod-Krai, an autonomous archipelago under Snezhnaya, sits on the very edge of the continent. Khaenri'ah lay deep underground beneath Sumeru.

Places: Besides the seven nations: Nod-Krai (Snezhnaya's autonomous borderland), fallen Khaenri'ah, Celestia in the sky and the Dark Sea beyond the continent.

People: Humans make up most of Teyvat's population, alongside adepti, spirits, Seelies (the cursed remnants of Angels), vishaps and other elemental creatures, hilichurls and Abyssal monsters. A Vision-holder is called an "allogene", someone said to have the potential to ascend to Celestia and become a god.

Governance: The world order works top-down. The Heavenly Principles rule from Celestia through the Four Shades (Rulers of Life, Death, Time and Space). The Seven govern the nations. Each Archon holds a divine throne in Celestia, made from an elemental Authority taken from a dragon Sovereign, and each received a Gnosis linking them to Celestia.

Economy: Mora is the currency accepted everywhere in Teyvat; its item text calls it the one language everybody speaks. It is named after Morax and could only be minted with the Geo Archon's power at Liyue's Golden House, which has stopped minting new Mora since Zhongli gave up the Geo Gnosis.

History: Teyvat's history in broad strokes:
- **The Old World:** dragons ruled under the Seven Sovereigns and their king, Nibelung, who raised Three Moons from the planet's crust.
- **The conquest:** the Heavenly Principles came from the stars, defeated the dragons, took their Authorities and built a human "unified civilization" guided by Angels.
- **The war of funerary flame, about 6,000 years ago:** Nibelung returned with the Abyss. The war shattered that civilization and two of the moons, and all history from before it was banned.
- **The Archon War, about 6,000 to 2,000 years ago:** gods fought for seven thrones, and The Seven and their nations emerged.
- **The cataclysm, 500 years ago:** Khaenri'ah fell and the Abyss spread across all seven nations.
- **The present:** the Traveler's journey through the seven nations in search of their twin.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Archon Quest is in Snezhnaya (Chapter VII). The Heavenly Principles still sleep. The Tsaritsa's Fatui hold six of the seven Gnoses and are openly preparing to challenge Celestia. The Frost Moon has returned to Teyvat's sky.

In 7.1 the Tsaritsa outmaneuvered the Shade Rhinedottir, and Celestia stripped Ronova of the Authority of Death for abusing it. Pierro's group then defeated Ronova. In her last act, the mortally wounded Ronova made the Celestial Nail over the Cryo Dragon's corpse crumble, threatening to spread Holy Soil across Teyvat. Every other Nail began to shine a strange light into the sky, visible to people everywhere.

71.content: Each of Teyvat's seven nations worships the Archon of one element, and that Archon's ideal shapes its government: Mondstadt (Anemo, freedom), Liyue (Geo, contracts), Inazuma (Electro, eternity), Sumeru (Dendro, wisdom), Fontaine (Hydro, justice), Natlan (Pyro, war) and Snezhnaya (Cryo, love). The nations were founded after the Archon War about 2,000 years ago, when the winning gods shaped their lands with their elemental power. Snezhnaya counts as independent, like Mondstadt, and it administers the autonomous borderland of Nod-Krai.

72.content: Celestia is a floating cluster of landmasses in the sky over Liyue, near Mt. Mingyuan. It has a great central spire, outer rocks linked by a ring, and rivers that pour off its edges and fade into nothing as they fall. People believe heroes ascend there to become gods. It is home to the Heavenly Principles and the meeting place of the Four Shades (Asmoday has been absent since the cataclysm). The Angels lived there until they were cast out. Venti claims its water tastes foul and its fruit is bland.

73.content: The "Dark Sea" is the umbrella name for everything beyond the continent and outside The Seven's rule, landmasses included. Gods defeated in the Archon War who refused the new order fled there. Enkanomiya, though it lies directly beneath Watatsumi Island, counts as Dark Sea because The Seven have no jurisdiction over it. Inazuma borders the Dark Sea.

74.content: Khaenri'ah was a nation built by humans with no god at all, deep underground beneath Sumeru. People from the seven nations joined it over the millennia. 500 years ago, monsters bearing the Abyss's power, created by the alchemist Rhinedottir, poured out of it across Teyvat. The Heavenly Principles and The Seven destroyed Khaenri'ah for its use of the Art of Khemia and Abyssal power. Its surviving pure-blooded people were cursed with immortality, and those of mixed or foreign blood were turned into monsters. The bitterness this left gave rise to the Abyss Order and the Fatui.

75.content: Mora is Teyvat's universal currency. A loading screen says none dispute its value. Mora is also a catalyst for physical transformation, which is why crafters use it. It is named after Morax, and only the Geo Archon's power could mint it at the Golden House in Liyue, which has minted no new Mora since Zhongli surrendered his Gnosis.

76.comment: The Sea of Flowers at the End

The Sea of Flowers at the End (also: Sea of Flowers at the End, Sea of Flowers of the End): The Sea of Flowers at the End is a place where Inteyvat flowers, the national flower of Khaenri'ah, bloom in full. The Traveler's sibling found it at the end of their long journey. The Traveler had once said they wished to find such a place in the universe, so its discovery moved the sibling to stop travelling with the Traveler and take up Teyvat's affairs.

It is not a place the player can visit. Everything known comes from the sibling's own words to the Traveler during the Sumeru-set Archon Quest World-Order Narration.

Description: The sea is made of Inteyvat flowers: five-petalled blooms, four white petals and one pale blue. The name is the sibling's, repeated in quotation marks as a proper name for the place.

History: During their travels between worlds, the Traveler told their sibling they wanted to find a place in the universe where Inteyvat flowers were in full bloom. At the end of the sibling's journey across Teyvat, the sibling found such a place: the Sea of Flowers at the End.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible and not visited by anyone shown in game as of 7.1. The Traveler has heard of it only through the sibling.

77.comment: The Sea of Flowers at the End: Sea of Flowers and the sibling
77.content: In World-Order Narration the Traveler's sibling names the Sea of Flowers at the End as the place where they stopped their journey, and links it to the Traveler's old wish to find a world where the Inteyvat flower bloomed in full. The sibling does not say where it is or what is there beyond the flowers.

78.comment: The Sea of Flowers at the End: Inteyvat
78.content: Inteyvat is the national flower of Khaenri'ah, with four white petals and one pale blue petal. Dainsleif tells of it wilting in two weeks and hardening when taken away from Khaenri'ah. The Traveler says the same flowers grow in their homeland; Lumine wears one in her hair. Emilie, a modern Teyvat resident, had never heard of it before being told by the Traveler.

79.content:
Tletl Ilhuicatl (also: Tletl Ilhuicatl realm layout): Tletl Ilhuicatl is the Natlan-themed Realm Layout, added in Version 5.3. The game places it high above a sea of clouds, where towering peaks bask in scorching sunlight and the air is full of endless heat. The name is Nahuatl, from words for 'fire' and 'sky'.

It is unlocked by buying the Scroll of the Fiery Firmament from Tubby at the Realm Depot after finishing Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn (the layout's own page names Home of the Hot Springs instead). Its mansion is the Natlan Dwelling: "Lofty Tower"; the four areas are Firecage, Blazebelt, Flamecrest and Sunridge.

Geography: Sunlit peaks and ridges over clouds, with long cliff-side terraces. Firecage and Blazebelt share an island at different heights; Flamecrest sits at the lowest elevation; Sunridge is a long strip overlooked by a cliff face.

Places: Firecage (Trust Rank 1): the lower starting area, with a Sub-Space Waypoint on the cliff above it and a seat beside a lantern on the westernmost cliff. Blazebelt (Rank 5): overlooks Firecage and has a balloon platform to Flamecrest. Flamecrest (Rank 7): a long, thin area; balloons run to Blazebelt (through a short canyon) and to Sunridge. Sunridge (Rank 9): long and thin, reached by balloon from Flamecrest.

Travel: Entered through the Serenitea Pot gadget once the scroll is used; inside, the hot air balloons run between areas. Chubby, who brought the scroll as a souvenir from Natlan, appears at one unlocked area on Fridays to Sundays.

Atmosphere: Hot, bright and open, with balloons and birds drifting overhead. It evokes Natlan's tribes and Phlogiston travel, but no war or Archon trial exists here.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 unchanged since 5.3; it remains quest-gated through the scroll.

80.comment: Tletl Ilhuicatl: Scroll of the Fiery Firmament
80.content: The item that unlocks Tletl Ilhuicatl: a woven scroll from Natlan depicting its landscapes, brought back by Chubby as a souvenir. It is bought from Tubby in the Realm Depot after Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn.

81.comment: Tletl Ilhuicatl: Phlogiston Hot Air Balloon Stops
81.content: In-game map text describes the stops as resting places formed by Adeptal Energy, landing grounds for the Phlogiston Hot Air Balloons favoured by Natlan's tribes. Players ride them to other areas of the realm.

82.content: The four areas of Tletl Ilhuicatl: Firecage (Trust Rank 1), Blazebelt (5), Flamecrest (7) and Sunridge (9).

83.comment: Tletl Ilhuicatl: Natlan Dwelling: Lofty Tower
83.content: The mansion furnishing supplied with Tletl Ilhuicatl; the game gives no lore beyond its name.

84.content:
Tower of Radiant Light (also: Brilliant Light Tower): The Tower of Radiant Light is a large tower in Luyang Academy, the painting gallery of the Temple of Space. The Traveler climbs it during the quest Long Live Life, in the effort to restore the Academy.

Its name is rendered as 明光楼 in Chinese, which translates literally as Tower of Brilliant Light.

Geography: The tower stands within the Liyue-styled compound of Luyang Academy, which is built on a small island. The painter Daozi says the direct path to it is barred, so the party must approach through the Abode of Resplendent Talent.

History: Daozi, freed from a painting early in Long Live Life, explains that the Academy cannot be restored until a particular painting is completed. Its title, as he gives it, is "Once the Heavenly Heart Emerges, the Four Horizons Fade to White", and in his words it should be possible to complete the missing part of it in the Tower of Radiant Light.

Dangers: Ink blots and flowing ink are harmful to touch, and the Domain Keepers of the Temple of Space guard the Academy. Neither is tied specifically to the tower beyond the chase that leads to it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Academy is restored and its painters are free; the tower has no further role in the story.

85.comment: Tower of Radiant Light: Hall of Painted Worlds
85.content: Daozi's plan for restoring Luyang Academy depends on a painting named "Once the Heavenly Heart Emerges, the Four Horizons Fade to White", which he says is Inazuman in its taste for names. The tower is where its missing part was expected to be completed.

86.content:
Twinning Isle: Twinning Isle is a limited-time island group in the northeast of the Golden Apple Archipelago, the summer-event map east of Mondstadt. In the 1.6 Midsummer Island Adventure it was a cluster of fog-wrapped islets and a central stage with a samurai puppet; in 2.8 Summertime Odyssey it held a castle of Night Ravens connected with Fischl's imagination.

The Immernachtreich of the 2.8 event is Fischl's imagined realm, and the Night Raven castle on Twinning Isle is where the event placed it on the map.

Geography: In 1.6 the main island held a teleport waypoint, a cave beneath it with notes for the quest A Trip Through Fog and Wind, wind currents to its heights and Hymnal Rings; a south island, southeast islets, a northeast rock with a cave, and a Nameless Islet reachable only through sea fog completed the group.

People: In 2.8 the isle's residents are Night Ravens: talkative and theatrical workers, guards, storytellers and a squire who hopes to become a knight like Sir Oz. They speak of the Traveler as having the Prinzessin's eyes, meaning Fischl's.

History: The Maguu Kenki on the Central Platform was, per the archipelago timeline, stolen by an Inazuma pirate crew about 500 years ago and later protected the islanders until it was damaged and went inactive. That crew's boat had split in two, and one group drifted to the southeast of Twinning Isle.

Dangers: In 2.8, hilichurls, slimes, a Pyro Abyss Mage and Eye of the Storm and Stonehide Lawachurl elites. In 1.6, Pyro Whopperflowers, Mitachurls, a Cryo Abyss Mage, Dendro slimes and the Maguu Kenki on the platform.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; limited to the 1.6 and 2.8 event runs.

87.comment: Twinning Isle: Twinning Isle Night Ravens
87.content: In Summertime Odyssey (2.8), Twinning Isle held a castle of Night Ravens connected with Fischl's imagined realm, the Immernachtreich; its stage and tower stayed under construction until the act Immernachtreich Apokalypse was cleared.
